fish.name: Mud Whistler
fish.flavor: Whistles a single flat note when pulled from the water. Nobody has taught it a second one, out of kindness.

fish.name: Fog Minnow
fish.flavor: Barely there at all. Hold one up to a lantern and you can read straight through it — mostly apologies.

fish.name: Candlefin
fish.flavor: Its dorsal fin glows like a tallow stub burning low. Swamp folk say each one is lit for somebody who never came home for supper.

fish.name: Bogwater Grinner
fish.flavor: Smiles constantly, which would be charming if it had fewer teeth. It has so many teeth.

fish.name: Knee-Knocker
fish.flavor: Lives among the cypress knees and headbutts anything that trespasses. Currently zero for four thousand against the trees.

fish.name: Wisp Chaser
fish.flavor: Follows will-o'-wisps with total devotion and no survival instinct whatsoever. The wisps find it a little embarrassing.

fish.name: Murkling
fish.flavor: A soft brown lump with opinions. Squeaks indignantly when caught, then forgives you immediately and completely.

fish.name: Puddle Haunt
fish.flavor: Turns up in puddles far too small to hold it, then vanishes the moment you fetch a witness.

fish.name: Lantern Guppy
fish.flavor: Carries a pinprick of warm light in its belly. A jarful makes a fine reading lamp and a terrible conscience.

fish.name: Sock Eel
fish.flavor: Explains every lost sock in the Isles. It is not sorry. It is very warm.

fish.name: Drizzle Darter
fish.flavor: Only bites when it's raining, drizzling, misting, or somebody nearby is crying softly.

fish.name: Moth-Eaten Bream
fish.flavor: Its scales are full of tiny holes, as if something has been nibbling it in a wardrobe. Smells faintly of cedar and long goodbyes.

fish.name: Gossip Carp
fish.flavor: Mouths words at you through the murk. Lip-readers report it knows things about the heron that the heron would rather it didn't.

fish.name: Tea-Stained Tetra
fish.flavor: The exact color of a forgotten cup of swamp-water tea. Steeps itself a little darker every day.

fish.name: Hushfish
fish.flavor: Sound stops working near it. Anglers describe landing one in perfect silence, then hearing every splash arrive at once on the walk home.

fish.name: Backwards Loach
fish.flavor: Swims tail-first everywhere it goes. It insists it isn't going backwards; everyone else is.

fish.name: Milkfog Gar
fish.flavor: A long pale shape that drifts through the fog banks slightly above the waterline. Ask it no questions and it will tell you no lies.

fish.name: Fiddler's Perch
fish.flavor: Twitches in perfect time to a jig that nobody is playing. On very foggy nights, some anglers swear they can almost hear it too.

fish.name: Second-Shadow Shiner
fish.flavor: Casts two shadows on the swamp bed: one for itself, and one for whoever it used to be.

fish.name: Doorstep Croaker
fish.flavor: Hauls itself up to swamp cabins on cold nights and croaks until it's let in. Makes an excellent, extremely damp houseguest.

fish.name: Witchbottle Minnow
fish.flavor: Round and green as old glass, with something small sealed inside that turns when you turn it. Whatever you do, don't shake.

fish.name: Yawning Mudgill
fish.flavor: Yawns so wide it briefly turns inside out, considers the new arrangement for a moment, then yawns its way back.

fish.name: Pallbearer Perch
fish.flavor: Travels in solemn processions of six, bearing a single lily pad between them. Nobody knows what's under the lily pad. Nobody lifts the lily pad.

fish.name: Marsh Marionette
fish.flavor: Hangs in the water from four faint threads that rise into the fog and do not stop. When it dances for you, try not to think about who's pulling.

fish.name: Stitchfin
fish.flavor: Sewn together from at least three different fish, none of which match. The seams are very neat. Somebody, somewhere, cared enormously.

fish.name: Foglight Angler
fish.flavor: Dangles a lure that looks exactly like a will-o'-wisp, which is rude, because will-o'-wisps look exactly like its lure. The lawsuit is ongoing.

fish.name: Thirteenth Toadfish
fish.flavor: Every toadfish clutch in the swamp hatches exactly twelve. This is the other one — from all of them, every single time.

fish.name: Vesper Koi
fish.flavor: Surfaces at dusk exactly where the chapel bell drowned a century ago, and rings the hour with a slap of its tail. It has never once been late.

fish.name: Ringkeeper Eel
fish.flavor: Wears a band of worn gold two-thirds down its body. It matches every wedding ring the swamp has ever swallowed, and it is not giving them back.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Toll
fish.flavor: Its scales are worn coins from kingdoms the fog took long ago. It will carry one thing across the swamp for you — but it decides what counts as a fair price.

fish.name: Hollowmere Bride
fish.flavor: A pale shape trailing fin-lace like a veil, still waiting at the sunken altar. Catching her is the easy part. Telling her the wedding isn't today is the hard part.

fish.name: Wicker Saint
fish.flavor: Woven from reeds and river-faith by nobody who will admit to it. On feast days its basket-ribs fill with small lights, and even the frogs go respectfully quiet.

fish.name: Grandfather Murk
fish.flavor: The swamp did not form around him; he seeped in first and the swamp followed. Speak clearly, mind your manners, and let him keep the hook — he collects them.

fish.name: The Lantern Warden
fish.flavor: Keeper of every wisp in the fen, it glides its rounds with a lamp of cold green fire. At midnight it counts its lights, and if one is missing, the whole fog holds its breath until the little flame is found.

fish.name: The Fen's First Dream
fish.flavor: Before the cypress, before the fog, before anything had a name, the water lay down and dreamt of being alive. It is dreaming still. Reel gently — everything you have ever caught here is something it imagined.
